extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH R03 (NIH Small Research Grant) applications, especially biomedical/microbiology investigators
extracted.subtask_description: A sample NIH Small Research Grant (R03) application and supporting PHS/SF424 forms showing required sections, formatting instructions, required attachments, biosketch rules, budget and checklist items, and project-specific experimental selection/prioritization criteria for a forward-genetics microbiology study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted educational use of application text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the application is copyrighted. The awardee provided express permission for NIAID to post this grant application and summary statement for educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material may be used for nonprofit educational purposes only, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and confidentiality handling
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will respond to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH must protect confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 Conformance / Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility: the sample has been reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have trouble accessing the content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) required fields completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete all required SF424 (R&R) application fields (Type of Submission, Date Submitted, Applicant Information, DUNS, EIN/TIN, Type of Applicant, Type of Application, Federal Agency, Descriptive Title, Proposed Project Dates, Congressional District, PD/PI contact info, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SF424 face page and associated fields must be completed accurately; many of these items are repeated in the PHS398 checklist for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Summary/Abstract describing current understanding, rationale, approach, and expected outcomes (e.g., brief description of aims, methods, and how results will be used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary should succinctly state what will be done and why; in this sample it describes use of forward genetics, insertional mutagenesis, high-throughput screening, classification of mutants, mapping, and prioritization for further characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Public Health Relevance Statement that explains how the proposed work addresses a public health problem (succinct relevance to disease burden, understanding, or therapeutic development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample: statement linking identification of virulence factors to improved understanding of Histoplasma pathogenesis and potential development of improved therapeutics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe available facilities and other resources (laboratory space, special rooms, computing resources, office space, and access to institutional cores / shared resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics (e.g., ft2 of lab space, HEPA-filtered rooms for BSL-2 work, number/type of computers, access to sequencing/core facilities) and describe the scientific environment and collaborative strengths of departments/centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment availability and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment relevant to the proposal (microplate readers, robotic liquid handlers, microscopes, PCR machines, gel documentation systems, incubators, safety cabinets, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which equipment is within the PI's laboratory and which are shared/core resources; major equipment relevant to proposed work should be emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects / Vertebrate Animals / Clinical Trial declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether human subjects, vertebrate animals, or clinical trials are involved and provide IRB/IACUC status and assurance numbers or explain exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer specific PHS 398/Other Project Information questions (Is the Project Exempt? Is IRB/IACUC review pending?).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan components
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Specific Aims, Research Strategy (Approach, Significance, Innovation as appropriate), and Bibliography & References Cited as attachments per PHS398 instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Strategy should include explicit aims and approaches; the Table of Contents in the sample shows placement and page numbers for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Biographical Sketches for Senior/Key Personnel following the PHS 398 format and content rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES. Include NAME; POSITION TITLE; eRA Commons user name; EDUCATION/TRAINING; A. Personal Statement; B. Positions and Honors; C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications; D. Research Support (ongoing and completed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Budget and indirect cost reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide modular budget(s) showing Direct Costs, Consortium F&A, Indirect Costs (type and rate), indirect cost base, and total direct & indirect costs for each budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cognizant agency and Indirect Cost Rate Agreement date where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist items (administrative disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to checklist items such as Inventions and Patents, Program Income, and Disclosure Permission Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete these items accurately; provide amounts/sources for anticipated program income and permission for government disclosure if application does not result in award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and feasibility: mutant library generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate feasibility and scale of proposed experimental library (e.g., plan to generate ~40,000 mutants requiring ~400 96‑well plates and achievable throughput of 8–10 plates/week to complete within ~1 year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete throughput estimates and logistic considerations to justify feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary screening selection threshold (intramacrophage proliferation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select mutants showing at least 50% reduction in intramacrophage yeast proliferation compared to virulent control for secondary screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plate-based RFP fluorescence time course and compare to on-plate virulent and attenuated controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary screening selection threshold (macrophage destruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select mutants showing at least a 50% reduction in the ability to destroy macrophages compared to the virulent control for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macrophage survival quantified by LacZ activity; expect overlap between collections identified by different readouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required on-plate controls for screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Include on each screening plate: (1) uninfected macrophages, (2) macrophages infected with non‑mutagenized parental RFP‑fluorescent yeast (virulent control), and (3) macrophages infected with a cbp1 mutant strain (attenuated control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls enable normalization and identification of attenuated mutants by comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenotype confirmation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm candidate mutant virulence phenotypes by re-infection assays in triplicate and at multiple multiplicities of infection (MOIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recover mutants from inoculum plates and repeat macrophage infections to validate initial screening results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial mapping screen for known virulence genes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapidly screen mutants by PCR for T‑DNA insertions in known virulence genes (CBP1, SOD3, CATB, SID1, SRE1, YPS3) to identify representatives of known factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows triage of mutants already implicating known virulence loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping disrupted loci methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Map novel T‑DNA integrations by TAIL‑PCR using primers directed outward from T‑DNA LB and RB ends, then BLAST PCR products to the reference genome to identify disrupted genes or promoters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map positions against gene models (e.g., from transcriptome sequencing) and identify multiple insertions where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of attenuated mutants by intramacrophage phenotype
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify attenuated mutants into mechanistic categories based on RFP fluorescence kinetics: entry defects (low initial RFP), survival defects (declining RFP), intramacrophage growth defects (static RFP), and lysis defects (increasing RFP but no macrophage killing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use growth kinetics and macrophage survival measures to define the stage at which pathogenesis is blocked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary prioritization based on severity and external growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank mutants secondarily by severity of intramacrophage growth defect (reflected by RFP fluorescence); mutants showing impaired growth outside macrophages should be lowered in priority for virulence‑mechanism follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritization should focus on mutants most likely to reveal virulence mechanisms rather than general growth defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization by gene identity and predicted features
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize candidates based on identity and predicted function: secreted factors (predicted by SignalP) and novel genes are high priority; use conservation among intracellular pathogens and preferential expression in pathogenic yeast vs mycelial phase as additional prioritization criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply BLAST, GO-term annotation, SignalP predictions, and transcriptome expression differences to score and select the top ~10% of virulence genes for further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and downstream mechanistic studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For prioritized genes, perform genetic complementation to link loss of virulence to the disrupted locus, confirm attenuation in an in vivo murine inhalational model, and further define defects using cellular markers of intramacrophage trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These follow-up experiments establish causality and provide mechanistic understanding of how the factor contributes to intracellular survival and pathogenesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of institutional/core expertise and collaborative environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Document interactions with departmental and center expertise (seminars, joint meetings, access to investigators with complementary skills) as part of the scientific environment supporting the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific faculty and centers and describe how their expertise and core services will contribute to project success.
